description: Verify that DUT drops an ARP Request whose proto_type is not IPv4 — receiver must reject unknown upper-layer families per RFC 826 §2.4 and emit no Reply
approach:
[Objective]
Negative case for ARP_26. proto_type tells the receiver which upper-layer addressing scheme is being resolved; if it isn't IPv4 (0x0800), the sender_ip / target_ip fields don't have IPv4 semantics and the packet must be dropped.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • proto_type  = some non-IPv4 value   ← unknown
   • target_ip   = (interpreted bytes that would map to DUT IP under IPv4)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no ARP Reply

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_unexpected_reply — DUT replied despite the unknown proto_type. Suggests the receiver checked target_ip without first validating the protocol family.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the Request — proto_type filter worked
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_reply: DUT replied despite unknown proto_type — family check missing
